items.front: Procedure: single motor circuit in five steps
items.back:
1. FLC from Table 430.248 (1φ) / 430.250 (3φ) — not the nameplate (430.6(A)(1))
2. Conductors ≥ 125 % FLC (430.22)
3. Branch SC/GF device ≤ Table 430.52 % of FLC: inverse-time breaker 250 %, dual-element fuse 175 %, non-time-delay fuse 300 %, instantaneous trip 800 % (1100 % Design B); next standard size up permitted (430.52(C)(1) Ex. 1)
4. Overloads from nameplate FLA: 125 % (SF ≥ 1.15 or rise ≤ 40 °C) else 115 % (430.32(A)(1))
5. Disconnect ≥ 115 % FLC (430.110), in sight (430.102)

items.front: Worked: 10 HP, 3φ 460 V motor (Table 430.250 FLC = 14 A), inverse-time breaker
items.back:
Conductors: 14 × 1.25 = 17.5 A → 14 AWG Cu at 75 °C (20 A) is permitted — the 240.4(D) small-conductor caps don't apply to motor circuits (240.4(G)); 12 AWG is the common field choice
Breaker max: 14 × 2.5 = 35 A → 35 A standard
Nameplate 13.2 A, SF 1.15 → overload trip ≤ 1.25 × 13.2 = 16.5 A
Disconnect ≥ 1.15 × 14 = 16.1 A

items.front: Worked: feeder for three 3φ 460 V motors — 25 HP (34 A), 10 HP (14 A), 5 HP (7.6 A), inverse-time breakers
items.back:
Feeder conductors: 125 % × largest + others = 42.5 + 14 + 7.6 = 64.1 A → 6 AWG Cu 75 °C (65 A) (430.24)
Feeder OCPD: largest branch OCPD + other FLCs; 25 HP breaker = 34 × 2.5 = 85 A → 85 + 14 + 7.6 = 106.6 A → do NOT round up: 100 A (430.62(A))

items.front: Worked: overload for a motor with nameplate 28 A, SF 1.0, 50 °C rise; what if it trips on start?
items.back:
SF 1.0 and rise > 40 °C → 115 % × 28 = 32.2 A max
If that won't carry the start: next higher size allowed, but ≤ 130 % (SF 1.0 / > 40 °C) or ≤ 140 % (SF ≥ 1.15 / ≤ 40 °C) (430.32(C))
Use nameplate current for overloads; table current for everything else

items.front: Worked: 45 kVA 3φ 480–208Y/120 V transformer — primary-only protection; then primary + secondary
items.back:
Primary I = 45,000 ÷ (1.732 × 480) = 54.1 A; secondary I = 45,000 ÷ (1.732 × 208) = 124.9 A
Primary only (≥ 9 A): 125 % × 54.1 = 67.7 A → next size up permitted (Note 1) → 70 A
Primary + secondary: primary ≤ 250 % = 135 A → 125 A (no rounding up on the 250 % value); secondary ≤ 125 % = 156 A → 175 A permitted (Note 1)
Currents < 9 A: 167 %; < 2 A: 300 % (primary only)

items.front: Transformer secondary conductor rules — the two you'll be asked
items.back:
10-ft rule (240.21(C)(2)): ampacity ≥ the load and ≥ the device it feeds; if outside the enclosure, ≥ 10 % of the primary OCPD × primary-to-secondary voltage ratio; single OCPD at the end
25-ft rule (240.21(C)(6)): ampacity ≥ ⅓ of primary OCPD × ratio; ends in a single OCPD
Secondary conductors are never protected by the primary device alone except 2-wire/3-wire delta-delta (240.21(C)(1))

items.front: Worked: hermetic A/C with RLA 24 A, LRA 118 A — OCPD and conductors
items.back:
Conductors: 125 % × RLA (or branch-circuit selection current if larger) = 30 A → 10 AWG Cu (440.32)
OCPD: ≤ 175 % × 24 = 42 A → 40 A; if it won't start, up to 225 % = 54 A → 50 A (440.22(A))
Nameplate 'maximum OCPD' and 'MCA' on the unit override your math (440.4(B), 110.3(B))

items.front: Worked: 4500 W, 240 V storage water heater (≤ 120 gal) — circuit and OCPD
items.back:
Treated as continuous (422.13): 4500 ÷ 240 = 18.75 A × 1.25 = 23.4 A
Conductors ≥ 23.4 A → 10 AWG Cu
OCPD for a single nonmotor appliance over 13.3 A: ≤ 150 % of its rating → 28.1 A; not a standard size → next size up permitted → 30 A (422.11(E)(3))
Answer: 30 A breaker, 10 AWG Cu

items.front: Motor disconnect — type and rating quick table
items.back:
Rated ≥ 115 % FLC (430.110(A)) or HP-rated ≥ motor HP
Types (430.109): motor-circuit switch rated in HP; molded-case breaker; molded-case switch; instantaneous-trip breaker in a listed combination controller; listed manual motor controller marked 'suitable as motor disconnect'
≤ ⅛ HP stationary: the branch OCPD may serve (430.109(B)); cord-and-plug ok for portable (430.109(F))
Controller disconnect in sight of controller; motor disconnect in sight of motor or lockable (430.102(B))

items.front: FLC quick-recall — 3φ 460 V and 1φ 230 V (memorize for speed, confirm in the table)
items.back:
3φ 460 V: 1 HP 2.1 · 3 HP 4.8 · 5 HP 7.6 · 10 HP 14 · 20 HP 27 · 25 HP 34 · 50 HP 65 · 100 HP 124
1φ 230 V: ½ HP 4.9 · 1 HP 8 · 2 HP 12 · 3 HP 17 · 5 HP 28 · 10 HP 50
At 230 V 3φ, double the 460 V value; at 208 V multiply the 230 V value by ≈ 1.1

Protected by an OCPD ≤ the panel rating, on the supply side (408.36); a 100 A panel on a 200 A feeder fails
3φ 4-wire delta 'high-leg' panels: high leg on phase B, marked orange (408.3(E), 110.15)
No 42-circuit limit — the count is per the panel's listing
MWBC breakers need a common trip or identified handle tie (210.4(B))

Fluorescent luminaires with double-ended lamps and ballasts: disconnecting means in sight or lockable — not required in dwellings (410.130(G))
Clothes closets (410.16(C)): surface incandescent/LED with enclosed source ≥ 12 in from storage; surface fluorescent ≥ 6 in; recessed (enclosed source) ≥ 6 in; luminaires identified for storage areas may sit in the storage space
Tubs/showers: no cord-connected, chain-hung, pendant or track luminaires within 3 ft horizontally and 8 ft vertically of the rim (410.10(D))

Neutral at switch locations (with exceptions)
Grip center ≤ 6 ft 7 in. above floor
Metal faceplates/yokes grounded
Switches not in wet locations unless in weatherproof enclosures

Where GFCI/AFCI/TR/WR would be required today → install that type
No EGC in box: non-grounding, or GFCI marked 'No Equipment Ground', or grounding-type on a GFCI with both markings

items.front: Receptacles in damp vs wet locations
items.back:
Damp: cover weatherproof when closed (no plug inserted)
Wet: in-use cover (weatherproof with plug inserted) + WR-listed receptacle

More than 5½ ft above the floor
Part of a luminaire or appliance
Dedicated appliance receptacle (not easily moved)
Non-grounding replacements (406.4(D)(2)(a))

Bathtub/shower zone: 3 ft horizontal, 8 ft vertical — no cord/chain/pendant luminaires or fans
Closet: surface incandescent/LED enclosed 12 in.; surface fluorescent 6 in.; recessed enclosed 6 in.

Waste disposer: 18–36 in.
Dishwasher / trash compactor: 3 ft to 6½ ft
Range hood / microwave-hood: 18 in. to 4 ft (422.16(B)(4))

items.front: Motor sizing — which current for what?
items.back:
Table FLC (430.247–250): conductors (125%), OCPD, disconnect (115%)
Nameplate FLA: overloads (125% if SF ≥ 1.15 or rise ≤ 40°C, else 115%)

Nontime-delay fuse: 300%
Dual-element time-delay fuse: 175%
Instantaneous-trip breaker: 800%
Inverse-time breaker: 250%
(Next standard size up permitted per 430.52(C)(1) Ex. 1)

In sight of the controller AND in sight of the motor (or lockable per exception)
Rated ≥ 115% of FLC, or hp-rated
'In sight' = visible and ≤ 50 ft

items.front: Transformer primary OCPD (≤1000 V, primary only)
items.back:
Primary ≥ 9 A → 125% (next size up OK)
2 to < 9 A → 167%
< 2 A → 300%
With secondary protection: primary 250%, secondary 125% (≥ 9 A)

≤ 112½ kVA: 12 in. from combustibles (or barrier / fully enclosed)
> 112½ kVA: transformer room of fire-resistant construction (exceptions for Class 155+ insulation)
Ventilation openings unobstructed

Disconnect within sight AND readily accessible from the unit
Conductors ≥ 125% of RLA or branch-circuit selection current
OCPD per nameplate 'maximum fuse/breaker' marking

Directory: specific purpose, not 'lights'
Supply OCPD ≤ panelboard rating
Feed-through / subfeed lugs allowed; back-fed breakers must be secured (408.36(D))

items.front: Worked: working-space depth — 480Y/277 V panel with grounded metal on the opposite wall; 208Y/120 V panel facing another live panel
items.back:
The table uses voltage TO GROUND
480Y/277 V (277 V to ground → 151–600 V row): Condition 1 = 3 ft · Condition 2 (grounded parts opposite) = 3½ ft · Condition 3 (live parts both sides) = 4 ft → 3½ ft
208Y/120 V or 120/240 V (≤ 150 V to ground): 3 ft in every condition → 3 ft
Width ≥ 30 in or the equipment width; height ≥ 6½ ft; doors must open 90°

items.front: Worked: terminal temperature — 90 °C THHN on a 60 A circuit with breaker marked 60/75 °C
items.back:
Circuits ≤ 100 A or 14–1 AWG: use the 60 °C column unless equipment is listed and marked for 75 °C (110.14(C)(1)(a))
Breaker marked 60/75 °C → 75 °C column: 6 AWG THHN = 65 A ✔ (90 °C 75 A can be used only for derating math)
Over 100 A or > 1 AWG: 75 °C column (110.14(C)(1)(b))

items.front: Reading a Code question — words that change the answer
items.back:
'shall' = mandatory; 'shall be permitted' = allowed; Informational Note = advisory only (90.5)
'Readily accessible' = quickly, no tools/ladders/locks (keys are OK); 'accessible (wiring)' = not permanently closed in
'In sight' = visible and ≤ 50 ft
'Dwelling unit' vs 'one-family dwelling' — a duplex is two dwelling units
'Ampacity' = continuous current without exceeding temp rating

Indoor: footprint of the equipment extended from the floor to 6 ft above the equipment or to the structural ceiling; no foreign systems (ducts, pipes) in that zone (110.26(E)(1)(a))
Sprinklers allowed if the space is protected; dripping protection required over the equipment
Outdoor: same 6 ft; equipment enclosures suitable for the conditions
Working space (110.26(A)) and dedicated space are two different requirements

Covers premises wiring, yards, carnivals, industrial substations, PV, EV... (90.2(A)); NOT utility-controlled installations, ships, mines, railway rolling stock (90.2(B))
AHJ interprets rules, approves equipment, grants special permission (90.4)
Listed equipment: internal wiring not re-inspected at install (90.7)
Maryland: PSI tests the NEC 2020 edition — verify the version on your test notice

Ch. 1–4: apply generally
Ch. 5–7: special — supplement or modify 1–4
Ch. 8: communications — independent unless referenced
Ch. 9: tables (mandatory where referenced)
Annexes: informational only

'Shall' / 'shall not' → mandatory
'Shall be permitted' / 'shall not be required' → permissive
Informational notes and annexes → explanatory, not enforceable

Accessible (equipment): reachable, not guarded by locked doors/height
Accessible (wiring): can be removed/exposed without damaging the building
Readily accessible: reach quickly — no climbing, obstacles, or ladders
Visible AND not more than 50 ft (15 m) away

Continuous load: max current expected for 3 hours or more
Ampacity: max current carried continuously without exceeding the temperature rating, under conditions of use
Overcurrent: any current above rated — overload, short circuit, ground fault

Circuits ≤ 100 A or 14–1 AWG: 60°C column (unless equipment marked 75°C)
Circuits > 100 A or larger than 1 AWG: 75°C column
90°C conductors: use the 90°C column only for derating math

0–150 V: 3 ft (all conditions)
151–600 V: Cond. 1 → 3 ft · Cond. 2 → 3½ ft · Cond. 3 → 4 ft
601–1000 V: 3 ft / 4 ft / 5 ft
Cond. 1: insulated/no live parts opposite · Cond. 2: grounded parts opposite · Cond. 3: live parts both sides

items.front: Working space width, height, dedicated space
items.back:
Width: 30 in. or equipment width, whichever greater; doors open 90°
Height: 6½ ft or equipment height
Dedicated space: floor to 6 ft above equipment or structural ceiling — no foreign systems

Install listed equipment per its listing/labeling instructions (110.3(B))
Neat and workmanlike manner (110.12); unused openings closed; no damaged equipment

Arc-flash warning on switchboards/panels/MCCs in other than dwellings (110.16)
Field-applied hazard markings durable (110.21(B))
Disconnects marked for purpose unless obvious (110.22)

items.front: Entrance to working space — 1200 A rule
items.back:
Equipment ≥ 1200 A and over 6 ft wide: an entrance ≥ 24 in. wide × 6½ ft high at EACH end (or an unobstructed exit / double working space)
Personnel doors within 25 ft: open outward with panic hardware (800 A+)

items.front: Branch circuit vs feeder vs service conductors
items.back:
Service conductors: utility point to service disconnect
Feeder: service equipment (or source) to the final branch-circuit OCPD
Branch circuit: final OCPD to the outlets

items.front: Procedure: box fill count (what counts as 1, 2, 0)
items.back:
Each conductor entering and spliced/terminated = 1; unbroken pass-through = 1; a loop ≥ 2 × the 300.14 free length = 2
Pigtails that never leave the box = 0
Internal cable clamps = 1 (largest conductor present), each support fitting (stud/hickey) = 1
Each device yoke = 2 (largest conductor on that yoke)
All EGCs together = 1 (largest EGC); 2020 adds ¼ allowance for each EGC beyond four
Multiply counts by Table 314.16(B)(1) volumes: 14 AWG 2.00 · 12 AWG 2.25 · 10 AWG 2.50 · 8 AWG 3.00 · 6 AWG 5.00 in³
items.note: Verify the 2020 wording in 314.16(B)(5) for the 'more than four EGCs' quarter-allowance; the rest is settled.

items.front: Worked: box for two 12-2 NM cables (with EGC) feeding one duplex receptacle, internal clamps
items.back:
Conductors: 4 × 12 AWG = 4
EGCs (all) = 1
Clamps = 1
Device yoke = 2
Total 8 × 2.25 in³ = 18.0 in³ → a 4 × 1½ square (21 in³) or a 3 × 2 × 3½ device box (18 in³) works; a 3 × 2 × 2½ (12.5 in³) does not

items.front: Procedure: conduit fill for mixed conductor sizes
items.back:
1. Table 5: area of each conductor (THHN: 12 AWG 0.0133 · 10 AWG 0.0211 · 8 AWG 0.0366 · 6 AWG 0.0507 · 4 AWG 0.0824 · 3 AWG 0.0973 · 2 AWG 0.1158 · 1 AWG 0.1562 in²)
2. Sum them
3. Table 4: column for the raceway type at 40 % (>2 wires), 31 % (2), 53 % (1); nipple ≤ 24 in → 60 % (Note 4)
4. Pick the first trade size whose allowed area ≥ the sum
Same-size wires only: Annex C is faster

items.front: Worked: EMT for 3 × 6 AWG THHN + 1 × 8 AWG THHN + 1 × 10 AWG THHN EGC
items.back:
3 × 0.0507 = 0.1521
+ 0.0366 + 0.0211 = 0.2098 in²
EMT at 40 % (Table 4): ¾ in = 0.213 ✔ · ½ in = 0.122 ✗
→ ¾ in EMT (tight; 1 in = 0.346 gives pulling room)

items.front: Worked: how many 12 AWG THHN in 1 in EMT (40 % = 0.346 in²)?
items.back:
0.346 ÷ 0.0133 = 26.0 → 26 conductors
Note 7: when the result's decimal is 0.8 or higher, round up (e.g., 15.8 → 16); below 0.8, round down
Annex C Table C.1 lists the same answer for same-size conductors

items.front: Procedure: ampacity with temperature + bundling corrections (worked: 8 × 10 AWG THHN in one conduit at 45 °C)
items.back:
1. Start at the conductor's insulation column: 10 AWG THHN 90 °C = 40 A
2. × temperature factor (Table 310.15(B)(1)(1), 90 °C column, 41–45 °C) 0.87 → 34.8 A
3. × adjustment (Table 310.15(C)(1), 7–9 conductors) 0.70 → 24.4 A
4. Final ampacity is the lesser of that and the termination column (110.14(C): 10 AWG → 60 °C = 30 A for ≤ 100 A circuits unless listed for 75 °C) → 24.4 A governs
5. 240.4(D) cap 30 A still applies to the OCPD

items.front: Worked: how many current-carrying conductors — 2 MWBCs (3-wire from a 120/240 V 1φ panel) + 1 × 120 V 2-wire circuit in one EMT?
items.back:
MWBC on 1φ 3-wire: neutral carries only the unbalance → not counted (310.15(E)(1)) → 2 each = 4
2-wire circuit: hot + neutral both count = 2
EGCs never count (310.15(F))
Total 6 → 80 % adjustment
On a 3φ 4-wire wye with ≥ 50 % nonlinear load, the neutral counts (310.15(E)(3))

items.front: Worked: THWN conductors in EMT lying directly on a rooftop (½ in above the roof) at 38 °C ambient
items.back:
2020 rooftop rule: raceways or cables less than ⅞ in above the roof add 33 °C (60 °F) → 38 + 33 = 71 °C design ambient
THWN is 75 °C insulation; Table 310.15(B)(1)(1) gives no 75 °C factor above 70 °C → the conductor can't be used there
Fix: raise the raceway ≥ ⅞ in above the roof (no adder), or use 90 °C conductors (THWN-2: 0.50 at 71–75 °C)
Exception: XHHW-2 is exempt from the adder

items.front: Temperature correction factors worth memorizing (75 °C and 90 °C columns)
Worked: smallest Cu conductor for a 150 A noncontinuous feeder, 75 °C terminations, no derating; same for aluminum
items.back:
Table 310.16, 75 °C column: 1/0 Cu = 150 A ✔
Al 75 °C: 3/0 Al = 155 A ✔ (2/0 Al = 135 A ✗)
Rule of thumb: Al runs about two sizes larger than Cu for the same ampacity

1/0 AWG and larger only (limited exceptions)
Each set: same length, material, size (CM), insulation type, terminated the same way
Each raceway or cable gets a full set, including an EGC sized per 250.122 for the OCPD
Ampacity = sum of the sets, then apply the adjustment factor for the conductor count in each raceway

items.front: Worked burial depths: UF cable for a 20 A 120 V GFCI-protected circuit to a lamp post; PVC under a residential driveway; RMC in a yard
items.back:
UF, 120 V ≤ 20 A with GFCI: 12 in (Table 300.5 column 4)
PVC under one-/two-family dwelling driveway: 18 in (column 3)
RMC/IMC: 6 in (column 2)
Direct-burial cable default: 24 in; under a 4 in concrete slab: 18 in

items.front: Worked: NM cable through bored holes in studs — hole edge 1 in from the stud face. OK?
items.back:
No: the hole edge must be ≥ 1¼ in from the nearest edge of the framing member, else a 1/16 in steel plate is required (300.4(A)(1))
Same 1¼ in for cables run parallel to framing (300.4(D))
Rigid metal, IMC, EMT and RMC don't need the plate

items.front: Support intervals — worked quiz: EMT, RMC ¾ in, NM, MC
items.back:
EMT: within 3 ft of each box, then ≤ 10 ft (358.30)
RMC: within 3 ft of boxes, then Table 344.30(B)(2): ½–¾ in 10 ft · 1 in 12 ft · 1¼–1½ in 14 ft · 2–2½ in 16 ft · 3 in and larger 20 ft
NM: within 12 in of boxes, then ≤ 4½ ft (334.30)
MC: within 12 in of terminations, then ≤ 6 ft (330.30)

items.front: Worked: pull box for a straight pull of 3 in conduit; angle pull with one 3 in and one 2 in in the same wall
items.back:
Straight: length ≥ 8 × largest raceway = 24 in (314.28(A)(1))
Angle/U pull: distance to opposite wall ≥ 6 × largest + sum of the others in that row = 18 + 2 = 20 in (314.28(A)(2))
Between raceways with the same conductor: ≥ 6 × largest = 18 in
Applies to 4 AWG and larger conductors

items.front: Underground run details that get asked
items.back:
Direct-buried cables/conduits emerging from grade: protected up to 8 ft above grade (300.5(D)(1))
All conductors of a circuit in the same trench/raceway (300.5(I))
Backfill: no rocks/sharp material against cables; sand or protection where needed (300.5(F))
Warning tape on underground service conductors not in raceway, ≥ 12 in above (300.5(D)(3))

Direct-burial cable/UF: 24 in.
RMC/IMC: 6 in.
PVC (no concrete): 18 in.
Residential 120 V ≤20 A GFCI branch: 12 in.
Under 4-in. slab, no vehicles: cable 18 / raceway 4 in.

Bored holes and parallel runs: ≥ 1¼ in. from the edge, or a 1/16-in. steel plate.
Notches: steel plate.
Under metal-corrugated roof decking: ≥ 1½ in. below.

≥ 6 in. from where the conductor emerges
≥ 3 in. outside the box opening (openings < 8 in.)
Not required for conductors passing straight through.

4–6 → 80%
7–9 → 70%
10–20 → 50%
21–30 → 45%
31–40 → 40%
41+ → 35%
EGCs never count; balanced neutrals don't count.

26–30°C → 1.00
31–35 → 0.96
36–40 → 0.91
41–45 → 0.87
46–50 → 0.82
51–55 → 0.76
Start from the conductor's own column; then check the termination limit (110.14(C)).

100 A → 4 Cu / 2 Al
125 A → 2 Cu / 1/0 Al
150 A → 1 Cu / 2/0 Al
200 A → 2/0 Cu / 4/0 Al
(one-family dwellings and individual units; main power feeder too)

14 AWG → 2.00 in³
12 AWG → 2.25
10 AWG → 2.50
8 AWG → 3.00
6 AWG → 5.00
Count: each conductor 1; all EGCs together 1 (2 if more than 4); internal clamps 1; each device yoke 2; fixture studs/hickeys 1 each.

items.front: Pull box sizing (4 AWG and larger)
items.back:
Straight pull: length ≥ 8 × largest raceway
Angle/U pull: ≥ 6 × largest + sum of other raceways on the same wall
Between raceway entries of the same conductor: ≥ 6 × largest raceway

1 conductor → 53%
2 conductors → 31%
3 or more → 40%
Nipple ≤ 24 in. → 60% (no derating)

items.front: THHN in EMT — common lookups (Annex C.1)

items.back:
RMC / IMC / EMT: within 3 ft of boxes, every 10 ft
FMC / LFMC: within 12 in., every 4½ ft
PVC: within 3 ft; spacing by size (Table 352.30) — ½–1 in. every 3 ft
ENT: within 3 ft, every 3 ft

Secure within 12 in. of boxes, every 4½ ft
Ampacity: 60°C column (12 AWG → 20 A, 10 AWG → 30 A)
Not in commercial garages, theaters, hazardous locations, or exposed in dropped ceilings of other than dwellings
Bundled through the same hole > 24 in. → derate

items.front: AC, MC, SE, UF — one-line IDs
items.back:
AC: armored, bonding strip, anti-short bushings; secure 12 in. / 4½ ft
MC: metal clad, needs listed fittings; EGC inside; secure 12 in. / 6 ft
SE: service-entrance; SER has a separate EGC; interior use per 338.10
UF: direct burial; 60°C ampacity like NM

Required where expected length change ≥ ¼ in. in a straight run.
Table 352.44: roughly 4 in. per 100 ft for a 100°F swing.

No substitute for fixed wiring
Not through walls, ceilings, floors, doorways, windows
Not attached to building surfaces (except 400.10(A)(1) exceptions)
Not concealed behind walls/ceilings
Not in raceways (except as permitted)

All conductors of a circuit — ungrounded, grounded, EGC — in the same raceway, cable, trench, or cord.
Prevents induction heating and keeps the fault path intact.

items.front: Worked: PV source circuit, 10 modules in series, Isc = 9.5 A — circuit current and conductor ampacity
items.back:
Max circuit current = 125 % × Isc = 11.9 A (690.8(A)(1))
Conductor ampacity ≥ 125 % × that = 14.8 A before corrections (690.8(B)(1)) — i.e., 156 % of Isc
OR ampacity ≥ 11.9 A after temperature/conduit-fill corrections — use the larger result (690.8(B)(2))
Series string: current stays 9.5 A, voltage adds

items.front: Worked: max PV system voltage for 12 modules in series, Voc = 45 V, lowest expected ambient −20 °C
items.back:
Table 690.7(A) factor at −16 to −20 °C ≈ 1.18 (when the module temperature coefficient isn't given)
12 × 45 × 1.18 = 637 V dc
One- and two-family dwellings: ≤ 600 V (690.7) — this fails; 11 modules = 584 V ✔ or use the module's own coefficient
Other buildings: ≤ 1000 V; up to 1500 V only where not on or in buildings
items.note: Confirm the Table 690.7(A) factor for −16 to −20 °C (1.18) and the 600 V dwelling limit wording in 2020 690.7. Method is settled.

items.front: Worked: 120 % rule — 200 A busbar, 200 A main, adding a PV breaker
items.back:
Allowed: main + inverter OCPD ≤ 120 % × busbar = 240 A
240 − 200 = 40 A max PV breaker, located at the opposite end from the main (705.12(B)(3)(2))
Inverter output 7.6 kW at 240 V = 31.7 A → 125 % = 39.6 A → 40 A breaker ✔ fits exactly
Alternative: sum of all breakers excluding main ≤ busbar rating (705.12(B)(3)(3))

items.front: Worked: EV charger rated 48 A continuous — branch circuit
items.back:
EVSE is continuous (625.41): 48 × 1.25 = 60 A → 60 A breaker, 6 AWG Cu 75 °C (65 A)
A 40 A EVSE → 50 A circuit; 32 A → 40 A
2020 625.42: load management systems may set the max to the managed value

Receptacles: ≥ 6 ft from the inside wall; at least one general-purpose receptacle 6–20 ft (680.22(A)); GFCI for 15/20 A 125 V receptacles within 20 ft
Pump motor: GFCI on 15/20 A 125–250 V 1φ outlets (680.21(C))
Wet-niche luminaires: top of the lens ≥ 18 in below the normal water level (680.23(A)(5))
Switches: ≥ 5 ft horizontally from the inside wall unless separated by a barrier (680.22(C))

items.front: Worked: receptacles at a patient bed location — general care vs critical care
items.back:
Category 2 (general care): ≥ 8 receptacles, at least one from the normal system and one from the critical branch, or from 2 critical branch transfer switches (517.18(B))
Category 1 (critical care): ≥ 14 receptacles, at least one normal + one critical branch (517.19(B)(1))
All hospital-grade, listed, identified

items.front: Transfer times and testing — worked recall
items.back:
Emergency (700): power available within 10 s (700.12); monthly testing/maintenance records (700.3)
Legally required standby (701): within 60 s (701.12)
Optional standby (702): no time limit; load calc per 702.4
Emergency wiring kept separate from other wiring (700.10(B))

items.front: Worked: Class I Div 1 conduit seals — where within what distance?
items.back:
Seal within 18 in of each enclosure containing arcing/sparking parts, or any conductor splice/terminal (501.15(A)(1))
Seal where conduit leaves the Div 1 area — within 10 ft of the boundary, no unions/couplings/boxes between the seal and the boundary (501.15(A)(4))
Conduit 2 in and larger entering enclosures with splices/taps: seal within 18 in (501.15(A)(1)(2))
Threaded RMC/IMC with ≥ 5 threads engaged (500.8(E))

Major repair garage, unventilated: Class I Div 2 up to 18 in above floor (511.3(C)); ventilated (4 ACH or 1 cfm/ft²) → unclassified
Pits without ventilation: Div 1
Minor repair, no fuel work: unclassified
GFCI on 125 V 15/20 A receptacles for tools, diagnostics, etc. (511.12)

Equipotential plane in concrete floors of livestock confinement areas and outdoor concrete areas where livestock stand and energized equipment is nearby (547.10)
GFCI: all 125 V 15/20 A general-purpose receptacles in areas with equipotential planes, outdoors, damp/wet locations, dirt confinement areas (547.5(G))
Site-isolating device at the distribution point (547.9)
Corrosion-resistant wiring methods; dust-tight boxes

Class I: gases/vapors · Class II: dust · Class III: fibers/flyings
Division 1: normally present · Division 2: abnormal conditions only
Zones 0/1/2 (gases) and 20/21/22 (dust) are the alternative system

Within 18 in. of enclosures with arcing/sparking devices (Div 1)
Where conduit leaves a Div 1 area (boundary seal)
Div 2: at boundary and at enclosures required to be explosionproof
Only explosionproof fittings between seal and enclosure

Major repair, no ventilation: Class I Div 2 up to 18 in. above the floor
Pits without ventilation: Div 1
With 4 air changes/hr (or ventilation per 511.3): may be unclassified
Minor repair garages: generally unclassified

General care (Cat. 2): 2 branch circuits (1 critical, 1 normal), ≥ 8 receptacles
Critical care (Cat. 1): ≥ 14 receptacles, at least 1 critical-branch circuit
All hospital grade

General receptacles ≥ 6 ft from inside walls; GFCI within 20 ft
Pump receptacle 6–10 ft, locking, GFCI
Luminaires: lens top ≥ 18 in. below water
Equipotential bond: 8 AWG solid Cu
Switches ≥ 5 ft from the water (680.22(C))

Max voltage: Voc × low-temp correction (Table 690.7(A) or coefficients)
Source circuit max current: 125% × Isc
Conductor sizing: 125% of that (690.8(B)) → 156% of Isc overall
Residential DC max 600 V (1000 V other)

Outside array boundary (> 1 ft): ≤ 30 V within 30 s
Inside array boundary: ≤ 80 V within 30 s, or listed PV hazard control system
Initiation device at the service or readily accessible location

Sum of main + inverter OCPD ≤ 120% × busbar rating
Inverter breaker at the opposite end of the bus; label required
200 A bus / 200 A main → 40 A inverter max
Alternative: 100% rule (sum of all breakers except main ≤ bus rating)

Emergency (700): 10 s, life safety, separate wiring
Legally required standby (701): 60 s
Optional standby (702): no time limit; transfer equipment still required
Fire-pump: Art. 695

One 20 A sign outlet at each entrance of a commercial occupancy, no other load
Signs need a disconnect within sight or lockable
Neon transformers/power supplies: 600.23/600.24

Class 1: up to 600 V, installed like power wiring
Class 2: power-limited at source, low shock & fire risk (thermostats, doorbells)
Class 3: power-limited, higher voltage than Class 2, shock risk
Keep Class 2/3 separate from power conductors

items.front: Ag buildings, mobile homes, RV parks — one-liners
items.back:
Ag (547): equipotential planes in livestock areas, GFCI on 125 V 15/20 A receptacles in listed areas, corrosion-resistant methods
Mobile home (550): 4-wire feeder, service equipment min 100 A
RV sites (551.71): every site 20 A · ≥ 70% with 30 A 125 V · 50 A 125/250 V on ≥ 20% of EXISTING sites and ≥ 40% of all NEW sites · every 50 A site also gets a 30 A

items.front: Worked: VD on a 1φ 120 V, 16 A load, 150 ft one-way, 12 AWG Cu (6530 cmil)
Worked: minimum CM to hold 3 % on 1φ 240 V, 30 A, 200 ft one-way, copper
Worked: 3φ VD — 480 V, 40 A, 300 ft one-way, 8 AWG Cu (16,510 cmil)
Worked: line current of a 3φ 480 V, 75 kVA load
items.back:
I = kVA × 1000 ÷ (1.732 × V)
= 75,000 ÷ (1.732 × 480)
= 75,000 ÷ 831.4 ≈ 90.2 A
Same formula sizes transformer secondaries: 75 kVA at 208 V → 208 A

items.front: Worked: current of a 1φ 240 V, 10 kW resistive heater; then with PF 0.8
items.back:
Resistive (PF 1): I = P ÷ V = 10,000 ÷ 240 = 41.7 A
With PF 0.8: I = P ÷ (V × PF) = 10,000 ÷ 192 = 52.1 A
Lower power factor → more amps for the same watts

items.front: Worked: 1φ transformer, 480 V primary → 120 V secondary, 60 A secondary load
items.back:
Ratio = 480 ÷ 120 = 4:1
Primary current = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 A
Check with kVA: 120 × 60 = 7.2 kVA; 7200 ÷ 480 = 15 A ✔
Voltage steps down, current steps up by the same ratio

items.front: Worked: input current of a 10 HP, 1φ 240 V motor at 85 % efficiency, PF 0.9 (theory, not the NEC table)
items.back:
Output W = 10 × 746 = 7460 W
Input W = 7460 ÷ 0.85 = 8776 W
I = W ÷ (V × PF) = 8776 ÷ (240 × 0.9) = 40.6 A
For 3φ divide by 1.732 × V × PF
NEC sizing still uses Table 430.248/430.250 FLC, not this math

items.front: Worked: a load draws 50 kVA with 40 kW — find PF, kVAR and the angle
items.back:
PF = kW ÷ kVA = 40 ÷ 50 = 0.80
kVAR = √(kVA² − kW²) = √(2500 − 1600) = 30 kVAR
θ = arccos 0.80 ≈ 36.9°
Adding capacitors cuts the kVAR, raises PF toward 1.0

items.front: Worked: series R = 30 Ω, XL = 40 Ω on 120 V — Z, I, PF
items.back:
Z = √(R² + XL²) = √(900 + 1600) = 50 Ω
I = V ÷ Z = 120 ÷ 50 = 2.4 A
PF = R ÷ Z = 30 ÷ 50 = 0.60 lagging
If XC were present: X = XL − XC before squaring

items.front: Worked: XL of a 0.1 H coil and XC of a 50 µF capacitor at 60 Hz
Worked: total resistance of 10 Ω, 20 Ω and 30 Ω in parallel
items.back:
1 ÷ Rt = 1/10 + 1/20 + 1/30 = 0.1 + 0.05 + 0.0333 = 0.1833
Rt = 1 ÷ 0.1833 ≈ 5.45 Ω
Always less than the smallest branch (10 Ω)
Two resistors shortcut: R1 × R2 ÷ (R1 + R2)

items.front: Worked: 120 V across 10 Ω + 20 Ω + 30 Ω in series — current and each drop
items.back:
Rt = 60 Ω; I = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 A everywhere
Drops: 20 V, 40 V, 60 V (sum = 120 V, Kirchhoff)
Power: 40 W, 80 W, 120 W — the biggest resistor dissipates the most in series

items.front: Worked: resistance of 500 ft of 10 AWG Cu (10,380 cmil) using K = 12.9
items.back:
R = K × L ÷ CM = 12.9 × 500 ÷ 10,380 ≈ 0.62 Ω
Ch. 9 Table 8 cross-check: 10 AWG uncoated Cu ≈ 1.21 Ω per 1000 ft → 0.61 Ω for 500 ft ✔
Double the length = double the R; double the CM = half the R

items.front: Worked: 208Y/120 V system, each phase load 20 A — line current and total kVA
items.back:
Wye: line current = phase current = 20 A; line voltage = 120 × 1.732 = 208 V
kVA = 1.732 × 208 × 20 ÷ 1000 = 7.2 kVA
(or 3 × 120 × 20 = 7200 VA — same answer)
Delta flips it: line current = 1.732 × phase current, line V = phase V

items.front: Worked: cost to run a 1500 W heater 8 h/day for 30 days at $0.15/kWh
items.back:
kWh = 1.5 kW × 8 h × 30 = 360 kWh
Cost = 360 × $0.15 = $54.00
Watts ÷ 1000 → kW; × hours → kWh; × rate → dollars

items.front: Worked: 120/240 V 3-wire with 18 A on L1 and 11 A on L2 — neutral current? And on a 208Y/120 V 3-phase 4-wire with 18 A / 11 A / 0 A?
items.back:
1φ 3-wire: neutral = difference = 18 − 11 = 7 A
3φ 4-wire (two phases loaded): In = √(a² + b² − ab) = √(324 + 121 − 198) = √247 ≈ 15.7 A
Three equal phase loads → neutral ≈ 0 (balanced)

items.front: Worked: a 120 V RMS sine wave — peak and peak-to-peak; a 170 V peak — RMS
items.back:
Peak = RMS × 1.414 = 169.7 V; peak-to-peak ≈ 339 V
RMS = peak × 0.707 = 170 × 0.707 ≈ 120 V
Meters read RMS; insulation sees peak

items.front: Worked: a 1200 W, 120 V appliance — current, resistance, and power if run at 240 V (same R)
items.back:
I = 1200 ÷ 120 = 10 A
R = V ÷ I = 120 ÷ 10 = 12 Ω
At 240 V: P = V² ÷ R = 57,600 ÷ 12 = 4800 W — doubling voltage quadruples power (and burns it up)

E = I × R
I = E ÷ R
R = E ÷ I

P = E × I
P = I² × R
P = E² ÷ R
I = P ÷ E

Current is the same everywhere.
Resistances add.
Voltage drops add up to the source voltage.

Voltage is the same across each branch.
Branch currents add.
Total R is less than the smallest branch: 1/Rt = 1/R1 + 1/R2 ...
Two resistors: product ÷ sum. Equal resistors: R ÷ n.

Peak = RMS × 1.414
RMS = Peak × 0.707
120 V RMS ≈ 170 V peak

items.front: Impedance of R and X in series
items.back:
Z = √(R² + X²)
Net reactance X = XL − XC
30 Ω R + 40 Ω XL → 50 Ω

items.front: XL and XC formulas — what happens as frequency rises?
items.back:
XL = 2πfL → rises with frequency
XC = 1 ÷ (2πfC) → falls with frequency

True power W = VA × PF
Apparent power VA = E × I
Reactive VAR = √(VA² − W²)
PF = W ÷ VA = cos θ

WYE: E(line) = 1.732 × E(phase); I(line) = I(phase)
DELTA: E(line) = E(phase); I(line) = 1.732 × I(phase)
480Y/277: 480 ÷ 1.732 = 277

Ep ÷ Es = Np ÷ Ns = Is ÷ Ip
kVA in = kVA out (ignoring losses)
Secondary current = VA ÷ Es (1-ph) or VA ÷ (1.732 × Es) (3-ph)

1 hp = 746 W
Input W = output W ÷ efficiency
Efficiency = output ÷ input

Single-phase: VD = 2 × K × I × L ÷ CM
Three-phase: VD = 1.732 × K × I × L ÷ CM
K ≈ 12.9 copper, 21.2 aluminum (75°C)
L = one-way length in ft; CM from Ch. 9 Table 8

3% for a branch circuit
5% total for feeder + branch circuit
(Informational — recommended, not mandatory)

items.front: Neutral current on a 120/240 V 3-wire circuit
items.back:
Neutral carries the difference between the two line currents.
20 A and 14 A → 6 A on the neutral.
Balanced 3-phase wye linear loads → 0 A.

Longer → more R (proportional)
Larger area (CM) → less R (inverse)
Hotter copper → more R
Material: copper lower than aluminum

Inductor (L): voltage E leads current I
Capacitor (C): current I leads voltage E
Pure inductive/capacitive → 90° shift

kWh = kW × hours
Cost = kWh × rate
1.5 kW × 8 h × 30 d = 360 kWh

Current law: currents into a node = currents out.
Voltage law: sum of voltage drops around any closed loop = source voltage.

items.front: Procedure: dwelling general lighting + small appliance + laundry (standard method)
items.back:
1. Floor area × 3 VA/ft² (Table 220.12)
2. + 1500 VA × 2 small-appliance circuits (220.52(A)) + 1500 VA laundry (220.52(B))
3. Apply Table 220.42: first 3000 VA @ 100 %, 3001–120,000 VA @ 35 %, rest @ 25 %
4. Add range (Table 220.55), dryer (220.54), fixed appliances (220.53, 75 % if ≥ 4), heat or A/C — larger of the two (220.60) @ 100 %

items.front: Worked: 2400 ft² dwelling — general lighting after demand
items.back:
2400 × 3 = 7200 VA
+ 3000 (small appliance) + 1500 (laundry) = 11,700 VA
First 3000 @ 100 % = 3000
Remaining 8700 @ 35 % = 3045
Demand load = 6045 VA

items.front: Worked: one 12 kW range; one 15 kW range; branch-circuit minimum
items.back:
≤ 12 kW, one range: column C = 8 kW demand
15 kW: 8 kW + 5 % per kW over 12 → 8 × 1.15 = 9.2 kW (Note 1)
Branch: 9200 ÷ 240 = 38.3 A → 40 A circuit; 210.19(A)(3) sets 40 A minimum for 8¾ kW and larger ranges anyway

items.front: Worked: dryer load and neutral for a 5.5 kW dryer
items.back:
Dryer: nameplate or 5000 VA, whichever is larger → 5500 VA (220.54)
Table 220.54: 1–4 dryers @ 100 %
Neutral for ranges/dryers: 70 % of the demand → 5500 × 0.70 = 3850 VA (220.61(B)(1))

items.front: Worked: optional method — 2000 ft² dwelling, 12 kW range, 5 kW dryer, 4.5 kW water heater, 5 kW A/C vs 10 kW electric heat
Worked: 60 general-purpose receptacles in an office — load and demand
items.back:
180 VA per yoke (220.14(I)) → 60 × 180 = 10,800 VA
Table 220.44 (nondwelling receptacles): first 10 kVA @ 100 %, remainder @ 50 %
10,000 + 400 = 10,400 VA
One quad = 2 yokes = 360 VA; a multi-outlet assembly is per 220.14(H)

items.front: Procedure: size conductor + OCPD for a continuous load (worked: 20 A continuous + 8 A noncontinuous)
items.back:
Minimum = 125 % × continuous + 100 % × noncontinuous
= 25 + 8 = 33 A
OCPD: next standard size ≥ 33 A → 35 A (240.6(A))
Conductor: ampacity ≥ 33 A after corrections; 10 AWG Cu 75 °C (35 A) works, but 240.4(D) caps 10 AWG at 30 A → 8 AWG

items.front: Worked: a conductor's corrected ampacity is 115 A — which OCPD? The rounding rules
items.back:
No standard size at 115 A → the next size up, 125 A, is permitted (240.4(B)) when: ≤ 800 A, not a multi-outlet branch circuit for cord-and-plug loads, and the conductor isn't already capped by 240.4(D)
Above 800 A: OCPD must be ≤ the conductor ampacity (240.4(C))
Standard sizes to recall (240.6(A)): 15 20 25 30 35 40 45 50 60 70 80 90 100 110 125 150 175 200 225 250 300 350 400 450 500 600

items.front: Worked: GEC for a 200 A service with 3/0 Cu service conductors; and if the only electrode is a ground rod
items.back:
3/0 Cu → Table 250.66 row '2/0 or 3/0' → 4 AWG Cu GEC
Rod/pipe/plate only: GEC never required larger than 6 AWG Cu (250.66(A))
Concrete-encased electrode only: not larger than 4 AWG Cu (250.66(B))
Parallel sets: add the CM of one phase to pick the row

items.front: Worked: EGC when 100 A feeder conductors are upsized from 3 AWG to 1 AWG Cu for voltage drop
items.back:
Base EGC for a 100 A OCPD = 8 AWG Cu (Table 250.122)
Upsize in proportion to circular mils (250.122(B)): 1 AWG 83,690 ÷ 3 AWG 52,620 = 1.59
8 AWG 16,510 × 1.59 = 26,258 cmil — just over 6 AWG (26,240) → 4 AWG Cu
EGC never needs to be larger than the circuit conductors (250.122(A))

items.front: Worked: supply-side bonding jumper for 600 kcmil Cu service conductors; and for 2 × 500 kcmil per phase
items.back:
600 kcmil Cu → row 'over 350 through 600' → 1/0 Cu
2 × 500 kcmil per phase = 1000 kcmil → row 'over 600 through 1100' → 2/0 Cu
Over 1100 kcmil Cu: jumper ≥ 12½ % of the largest phase conductor area (Table 250.102(C)(1) Note 1)
Parallel sets: add the areas of one phase to pick the row

items.front: Worked: 200 A dwelling service — minimum conductor using the 83 % rule
items.back:
200 × 0.83 = 166 A required ampacity (310.12(A), services 100–400 A to a single dwelling)
Table 310.16, 75 °C: 2/0 Cu = 175 A ✔ (vs 3/0 without the rule)
4/0 Al = 180 A ✔
Feeder to the whole dwelling load qualifies too (310.12(B))

10-ft tap: ampacity ≥ calculated load AND ≥ the device it feeds; if leaving the enclosure, ≥ 10 % of the feeder OCPD; ends in a single OCPD or device; in a raceway
25-ft tap: ampacity ≥ ⅓ of feeder OCPD; ends in a single OCPD rated ≤ tap ampacity; protected from damage
Worked: 400 A feeder → 25-ft tap needs ≥ 133 A (1/0 Cu at 150 A)

items.front: Worked: biggest cord-and-plug load on a 20 A receptacle; receptacle choices on a 30 A circuit
items.back:
Single cord-and-plug load ≤ 80 % of the receptacle rating: 20 A → 16 A; 15 A → 12 A; 30 A → 24 A
30 A branch circuit (2+ receptacles): 30 A receptacles only
20 A circuit: 15 or 20 A receptacles; 15 A circuit: 15 A only; 40/50 A circuit: 40 or 50 A

items.front: Worked: feeder neutral for a 500 A unbalanced load (no nonlinear loads)
items.back:
First 200 A @ 100 % = 200
Remainder 300 A @ 70 % = 210
Neutral demand = 410 A
No reduction for the portion from nonlinear loads or for 3-wire 1φ from a 4-wire 3φ wye (220.61(C))

items.front: Worked: feeder for 60 A continuous + 40 A noncontinuous
items.back:
Conductor: 125 % × 60 + 40 = 115 A min (215.2(A)(1))
OCPD: same 115 A min → 125 A standard (215.3, 240.6)
If the OCPD is 100 %-rated and listed: conductors and OCPD at 100 % (exception)
Table 310.16 75 °C: 1 AWG Cu = 130 A ✔

Service conductors sized to the calculated load per Art. 220 (230.42(A)); continuous loads × 125 %
Disconnect rating: one-family dwelling ≥ 100 A (230.79(C)); 2 circuits ≥ 30 A; one circuit ≥ 15 A; everything else ≥ 60 A
Max 6 disconnects — 2020: each in its own enclosure or compartment (230.71)

No point along the floor line more than 6 ft from a receptacle → max 12 ft apart.
Wall spaces 2 ft or wider count. Floor receptacles within 18 in. of the wall count.

Any wall counter space 12 in. or wider gets one.
No point along the wall line more than 24 in. from a receptacle (4 ft apart max).
Islands/peninsulas: 2020 — at least one per island/peninsula (per 9 sq ft rule).

Bathrooms · garages & accessory buildings · outdoors · crawl spaces · basements · kitchens (countertop) · within 6 ft of any sink · boathouses · within 6 ft of bathtub/shower · laundry areas · indoor damp/wet locations

Kitchens, family rooms, dining, living, parlors, libraries, dens, bedrooms, sunrooms, rec rooms, closets, hallways, laundry areas, similar.
NOT: bathrooms, garages, outdoors, unfinished basements.

2 small-appliance (kitchen/dining)
1 laundry
1 bathroom
1 garage (attached garages, 2017+)

Conductors and OCPD ≥ 125% of continuous + 100% of noncontinuous.
Continuous = 3 hours or more.

items.front: Receptacle ratings permitted per circuit (2+ receptacles)
items.back:
15 A circuit → 15 A
20 A → 15 or 20 A
30 A → 30 A
40 A → 40 or 50 A
50 A → 50 A

Outdoor: front & back, ≤ 6½ ft above grade
Garage: one per vehicle bay, ≤ 5½ ft above floor
Hallway: 10 ft or longer → at least one
Bathroom: within 3 ft of basin edge

General lighting: 3 VA per sq ft
Small appliance: 1,500 VA each (×2)
Laundry: 1,500 VA

Dryer: 5,000 W or nameplate, whichever larger
Range ≤ 12 kW (one): 8 kW (Table 220.55 Col. C)
Over 12 kW: add 5% per kW above 12

General loads: first 10 kVA at 100%, remainder at 40%
Then add largest of heating/cooling per 220.82(C)
Service must be ≥ 100 A

10 ft above grade at the service entrance (≤150 V to ground)
12 ft over residential property/driveways (≤300 V)
15 ft over commercial areas with truck traffic (>300 V)
18 ft over public streets, alleys, parking lots
8 ft above roofs (with exceptions)

Location: outside, or inside nearest point of entrance; never in a bathroom
Max six disconnects, each in its own enclosure (2020)
Min rating: one-family dwelling 100 A 3-wire; other 60 A

14 AWG Cu → 15 A
12 AWG Cu → 20 A
10 AWG Cu → 30 A
12 AWG Al → 15 A
10 AWG Al → 25 A

Allowed when: conductor ampacity isn't a standard rating, the OCPD is 800 A or less, and it's not a multioutlet receptacle circuit.
65 A ampacity → 70 A breaker OK.

10 ft: tap ampacity ≥ load AND ≥ OCPD rating at termination; ≥ 1/10 of feeder OCPD
25 ft: tap ampacity ≥ 1/3 feeder OCPD, ends in a single OCPD
All: protected from damage, in raceway

Readily accessible; handle ≤ 6 ft 7 in. above floor
Not near easily ignitable material (clothes closets)
Not in dwelling bathrooms
Not over steps of a stairway

Service conductor 2 AWG or smaller → 8 AWG
1 or 1/0 → 6
2/0 or 3/0 → 4
Over 3/0 to 350 kcmil → 2
Over 350 to 600 → 1/0
Over 600 to 1100 → 2/0
Over 1100 → 3/0
Rod/pipe/plate max 6 AWG; Ufer max 4 AWG

15 A → 14
20 A → 12
30, 40, 60 A → 10
100 A → 8
200 A → 6
300 A → 4
400 A → 3
500 A → 2
600 A → 1
Upsize proportionally when conductors are upsized for VD.

≥ 8 ft long, driven full length
Single rod OK only if ≤ 25 Ω; otherwise add a second
Rods ≥ 6 ft apart
Ufer: 20 ft of ½-in. rebar or 20 ft of 4 AWG bare Cu, 2 in. of concrete

items.front: Where is the neutral bonded to ground?
items.back:
Once — at the service disconnect (main bonding jumper).
Never on the load side (subpanels, separate buildings).
Separate building: run an EGC with the feeder; isolate the neutral; still install a grounding electrode.

items.front: Raceways that count as an EGC
items.back:
RMC, IMC, EMT: yes, as-is
FMC (250.118(5)): listed fittings, OCPD ≤ 20 A, ≤ 6 ft of flex in the fault path; add an EGC where used for flexibility
LFMC (250.118(6)): ⅜ and ½ in. → OCPD ≤ 20 A; ¾ through 1¼ in. → OCPD ≤ 60 A (no smaller LFMC in the path); ≤ 6 ft total
PVC, ENT, LFNC: never

Grounded (neutral): white, gray, or 3 white stripes
EGC: green, green/yellow stripes, or bare
Ungrounded: any other color (orange = high leg, 110.15)

Same breakpoints as Table 250.66 for ≤ 1100 kcmil.
Over 1100 kcmil Cu: 12½% of the largest ungrounded conductor area.
500 kcmil service → 1/0 Cu jumper.

Shared neutral, ungrounded conductors on different phases/legs.
Must have a simultaneous disconnect (handle tie or multipole breaker) at the origin.
Conductors grouped in the panel.

items.front: When are service conductors 'outside' a building?
items.back:
Under ≥ 2 in. of concrete beneath the building
In ≥ 2 in. of concrete or brick within the building
In a vault
In conduit under ≥ 18 in. of earth beneath the building
In an overhead service mast
